scope: Proposition 8.5 (Smooth tester and distance) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 90-91. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each fixed template, the canonical encodings of valid extended labels have constant relative distance. They admit a perfectly complete bounded-bit 90 tester with the following uniform gap: for every fixed a > 0, there are θ(a) > 0 and a size cutoff such that rejection below θ(a) implies distance less than a from one canonical valid word. Each potential raw read on each fixed answer branch has bounded density relative to the balanced word, without conditioning on execution of that branch. Consequently rejection is at most a fixed constant times distance from a canonical valid word.
